Workforce demographic statistics (gender, race, disability, LGBTQIA+, 70+ nationalities) are disclosure only and were not counted as activity. The pay equity analysis is biennial, with the next one in 2026. The company says supplier and hiring decisions are made on merit. Platform support for multiple languages/geographies and international sales were not counted (international-operations trap). Trap terms excluded: 'Innovative Technology', engineering 'design', ML 'content', 'brand equity', and 'Community' meaning customer operations teams. The Item 7 excerpt only repeats the overview sentence and adds no evidence. Some Impact details (climate index, SASB, EEO-1) are referred to the IR website, but coverage in Item 1 is enough to judge all themes. The $30M Impact Investment Fund (E6) is the source of the $3M Hope Enterprise investment (E5) and a $3M clean-energy loan; these were not double counted. Environmental activities were not scored except where they independently meet a theme (seller disaster relief).

JPM.notes: Community and Cross-cultural coverage marked insufficient, which triggers the automated sustainability-report second look. The 10-K says almost nothing about external community programs, and inclusion is limited to demographics. The $1.0 billion Visa-share contribution to the JPMorgan Chase Foundation was recorded in Q2 2024 and is marked past. The MD&A notes its absence in FY2025, so it does not raise the score. The Public Responsibility Committee oversees 'community investment', but this is governance language and is not scored. The MD&A line 'Credit for U.S. small businesses $2.9 trillion' appears to be a garbled table extraction: the $2.9 trillion likely refers to total credit and capital for all clients, so it was not used as a small-business indicator. The following were treated as traps and not counted: 'Consumer & Community Banking' (segment name), 'Community Reinvestment Act' (regulatory), mandatory compliance and conduct training, and client fraud-awareness education (a risk control, similar to customer education). Item 7 was read only as targeted excerpts.

WFC.notes: The Human Capital section is short and covers only employee pay, benefits, development and work-life matters. Item 1 says nothing about philanthropy, a foundation, external education or community investment, and it incorporates additional information by reference to the 2025 Annual Report to Shareholders. Community and Cross-cultural are therefore marked insufficient and should get the automated second look using the sustainability report. The $200 million development figure includes required risk and regulatory compliance training, which cannot be separated out. This does not change the score, because the employee-development cap of 2 applies either way. These items were checked and excluded as non-qualifying: the Community Reinvestment Act, which appears only as regulatory description; 'communities' in the Item 7 Risk and Culture paragraph, which is culture language; 'diversified' products; 'stockholders' equity'; international operations; and the technology/'innovations' references in the Competition section. The Item 7 excerpt describing Consumer Banking and Lending as serving consumers and small businesses is the same small-business lending activity as E5, so it is not counted twice. Item 7 references counts of digital/mobile active consumer and small business customers, but the excerpt contains no figures. The filing also discloses an ongoing FRB consent order (asset cap removed June 2025) and an OCC formal agreement on AML/sanctions. These are recorded for context only and are not scored.

XOM.notes: Human capital disclosure is a few general sentences, and the Item 7 excerpts contain no qualifying community or inclusion content, so Community and Cross-cultural coverage is insufficient. This triggers the automated second look using the company's latest sustainability report. Trap terms excluded: 'foundation' in Item 7 refers to the Global Outlook as the foundation for Corporate Plan assumptions, not a charitable foundation. ProxximaTM resin systems and carbon materials are industrial products, not creative work. The company's own research programs and over 8 thousand patents are its own innovation. The ladder places own innovation at level 1, but it does not enable other ventures and the 'innovation' trap applies, so I chose the lower level and Entrepreneurship is 0. For Community, the 30-year average service figure measures retention, not the reach of a development program.
